editorial_contributions.text: Let \(Q^ d\) be the set of all the rational points of the euclidean \(d\)- space, and let \(G(Q^ d)\) be the graph whose vertex-set is \(Q^ d\), where two points are adjacent if they are at distance one. It was shown in \textit{D. R. Woodall} [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A 14, 187-200 (1973; Zbl 0251.50003)] that \(\chi(G(Q^ 2))=2\), in \textit{M. Benda} and \textit{M. Perles} [Colorings of metric spaces (unpublished)] that \(\chi(G(Q^ 3))=2\) and \(\chi(G(Q^ 4))=4\), and in the author's paper [Aequationes Math. 37, No. 2/3, 259-266 (1989; Zbl 0705.05033)] that \(\chi(G(Q^ 5))\geq 4\), \(\chi(G(Q^ 6))\geq 6\), \(\chi(G(Q^ 7))\geq 8\) and \(\chi(G(Q^ 8))\geq 9\). In the paper under review, the author improves his previous result by raising each of his four lower bounds by one.

title.title: On the chromatic number of some rational spaces

editorial_contributions.text: The distance \(\text{dist}(x,y)\) in the graph \(G\) of rational points in the Euclidean space \(E^ d\) is studied; two points are connected by an edge iff their Euclidean distance is one. It is known that \(G\) is connected for \(d \geq 5\). The author shows that, for \(d \geq 8\), \(\text{dist}(x,y)\) cannot exceed the Euclidean distance by more than one.

title.title: Uniform distances in rational unit-distance graphs

editorial_contributions.text: First, the author recalls some sufficient conditions for a unit-distance preserving mapping from the Euclidean rational \(d\)-space \(Q^{d}\) into itself to be an isometry. Then, for an arbitrary subset \(A\) of the Euclidean space \(E^{n}\), he introduces the notion of the rational dimension \(\rho (A)\) of \(A\) as the least \(m\) for which a rational subset \(Q^{m}\subset E^{n}\) contains a congruent copy of \(A\). The author shows that if the vertex set \(S\) of a \(d\)-simplex \(\Delta^{d}\) in \(E^{n}\) has the property \(\| x-y\| ^2\) is a rational number for all \(x,y \in S\), then \(\rho(S)\leq 4d\). He also proves that if the set \(A\subset E^{n}\) has the same property \(\| x-y\| ^2\) is a rational number for all \(x,y \in A\) and if \(\dim (\text{Aff}(A))=d\), then \(\rho(A)\leq 4d\).

title.title: The rational analogue of the Beckman-Quarles theorem and the rational realization of some sets in \(E^d\)

editorial_contributions.text: The Beckmann-Quarles theorem asserts that for \(d > 1\) every mapping from a \(d\)-dimensional real space \(R^d\) into itself preserving the unit distance (`unit-preserving', i.e. pairs of points with distance 1 will be mapped into pairs of points, again with distance 1) will preserve any distance and hence is an isometry. For the rational case \(Q^d\) the same proposition is not a foregone conclusion. For some numbers \(d\) the matter has already been settled; the author adds the proof for the case of dimensions \(d = 2 n^2-1\) for \(n > 2\). This proof is indeed versatile as it can also be applied to several other cases.

title.title: The Beckman-Quarles theorem for rational spaces

editorial_contributions.text:
Let \(A=\{4k(k+1):k=1,2,3,\dots \} \cup (\{k^2: k=1,2,3,\dots \} \cap \{2k^2-1: k=2,3,4,\dots \})\). The author proves: if \(n \in A\) and \(x,y \in \mathbb Q^n\), then there exists a finite set \(\{x,y\} \subseteq S_{xy} \subseteq \mathbb Q^n\) such that for every unit-distance preserving mapping \(f:S_{xy} \to \mathbb Q^n\), \(\|f(x)-f(y)\|=\|x-y\|\) holds. 


The theorem for \(n=8\) was earlier proved by \textit{A. Tyszka} [Aequationes Math. 62, No. 1-2, 85-93 (2001; Zbl 1004.51023)].

title.title: A discrete form of the Beckman-Quarles theorem for rational spaces

editorial_contributions.text: Let \(Q^ p\) denote the collection of all the rational points of the p- space \(E^ p\), and let \(G(Q^ p)\) denote the graph, obtained by taking \(Q^ p\) as the vertex set, and connecting 2 points iff they are at a distance 1 (the usual Euclidean distance). There is shown that in every 4-colouring of \(G(Q^ p)\) every colour is everywhere dense. The chromatic number of \(G(Q^ 6)\), \(G(Q^ 7)\) and \(G(Q^ 8)\) is at least 6, 8 and 9, respectively.

editorial_contributions.text:
The authors prove a typical Beckman-Quarles theorem, namely: If \(Q^d\) denotes the rational \(d\)-space then, for any \(d\geq 6\), every unit-distance preserving mapping \(f: Q^d\to Q^d\) is an isometry.
